analyst_view.overall: A close one on paper: Chelsea fifth under Xabi Alonso after losing at Sunderland before the break, Leeds ninth under Daniel Farke after a 1-0 win over Tottenham and with a settled XI (same eleven three games running). Chelsea are without Reece James and Lacroix, with João Pedro (thigh, 'slight chance'), Hato and Jamie Gittens (ankle, hurt with England Under-21s) major doubts and Caicedo a minor doubt after Ecuador duty; the numbers already count João Pedro, Lacroix and Hato as out but not Gittens. Leeds have only Mateo Joseph out (counted), with Stach (foot, about 50%) and Gudmundsson (expected back in training) doubts. Michael Oliver referees, at exactly the league average for cards (counted).

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals and already remove João Pedro (about -19% on Chelsea's goals). Gittens, another forward, is a major doubt the numbers don't know about, and Caicedo's knock could weaken Chelsea's control; a small chance João Pedro plays pulls the other way, so only a slight trim, to about 2.45.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners. Chelsea's wing-backs and Palmer drive most of their corners, and Leeds' 3-4-3 with wing-backs is settled; without Gittens Chelsea lose a dribbler but keep the same width, so I stay at about 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.7 cards, already counting Michael Oliver (4.0 a game over 84 games) and Leeds' recent rise in bookings. Farke wants to avenge the 6-3 Carabao Cup loss to Chelsea in September, but that is ordinary motivation and neither side has suspensions; about 4.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.4 shots. Chelsea's thinner forward line (Gittens doubtful on top of the counted João Pedro, with Welbeck expected up front) trims their volume a little, so about 23.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.0 shots on target. Same reason, Chelsea short of a fit first-choice forward beyond what is counted: about 8.8.
